key_insight: Channel-wise Vector Quantization (CVQ) replaces patch-wise tokens with tokens per channel, quantizing each channel of a feature map so an image is represented as discrete levels of visual detail instead of a spatial grid.
problem_solved: Conventional patch-wise vector quantization ties discrete tokens to spatial patches, which can limit representational granularity and efficiency for autoregressive image modeling; CVQ addresses this by tokenizing along channels to better capture per-channel detail and dependencies.
method: Quantize each channel of a convolutional feature map into a small set of discrete levels (channel-wise codebook) instead of quantizing whole spatial patch vectors.
Represent images as sequences of channel-level tokens that encode visual detail per channel rather than a grid of patch tokens.
Train a visual autoregressive model that predicts the next channel token in sequence (next-channel prediction) to model cross-channel dependencies and enable generation/tokenization.
impact: CVQ provides a new, compact tokenization paradigm that can improve how models represent and generate images, enabling alternative autoregressive architectures and potentially more efficient downstream tasks like compression, generation, and conditional modeling.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: patch-wise tokenization vs. channel-wise tokenization to show the conceptual shift.
Pipeline flowchart: feature extraction → per-channel quantization → channel-token sequence → autoregressive next-channel prediction.
Heatmap / bar-chart: example feature map channels and their discrete quantized levels to illustrate information per channel.
Sequence diagram: autoregressive generation over channels (timeline of predicted channel tokens) to visualize dependency modeling.
paper_authors: Wei Song, Tianhang Wang, Yitong Chen, Tong Zhang, Zuxuan Wu
